![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14060128/assets/fec5c3e96eeed9fb01479c0127e2d530a628855a124d8ab1ef380c48c2f569f1.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $LMNL,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={C}_{1}\cup {-{C}_{2}}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{2}$ is the same path as ${C}_{2}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$
